known_weaknesses: LPs are structurally subsidisers. LMSR expected LP loss is about b · E[ln(p_lock(k*) / π(k*))]. Fees cover it only with volume of several times F. The fee ramp and the lock reduce this but do not remove it. Advertised 'yield' can be negative over many rounds, and first-loss LPs can lose 100% in one round.

Depth is fixed at open: b is constant. A market that goes viral after opening stays shallow, so big stakes move the odds sharply and get poor multiples. The only relief is a deeper seed in the next round.
The LP zone is a fee and first-loss tranche. It does not concentrate depth. Every bucket has the same b. A judge expecting Uniswap-v3-style concentrated depth will notice.

Tranche equilibrium is untested. If all LPs hide in tail zones, the waterfall degenerates to a pro-rata pool and fees on uncovered buckets flow to V. That is harmless, but the 'choose where' game may collapse to one or two dominant strategies.

Fixed grid. Resolution is δ per bucket and the outcome space is frozen at creation. A large move parks the price in a tail bucket, where all accuracy distinctions vanish. A bad σ guess by the creator produces a dull market.
Prior mis-specification is a free gift to the first traders, bounded by b · KL(truth ‖ prior), and LPs pay it. A uniform prior is worst here.

Bucket-edge sensitivity. Settlement is a single tick. The earliest-tick rule removes the cranker's discretion, but a price sitting on an edge at T makes payouts knife-edge. Pyth confidence intervals are ignored.
Equity feeds. If T falls outside publishing hours the market voids to lock prices. The creator must choose T sensibly, because the chain cannot validate trading calendars.

Liveness reverts. The price floor of 2^-24 and the V ≥ max L assert can reject extreme buys. These are liveness limits, not solvency risks, but a whale can make far buckets temporarily unbuyable by others only at real cost to the whale.

Numerical assumptions. Solvency relies on exp and ln implementations with a certified one-sided error. The +1 unit padding assumes b < 2^62 base units and an ln error < 2^-60. This needs a property test against a bignum reference.

Positions are PDAs, not SPL tokens. There are N(N+1)/2 shapes multiplied by the ring stacks, which is too many mints. They are transferable by instruction but not plug-and-play collateral in existing DeFi.
MEV. Buys and sells can be sandwiched within max_total / min_out. The ramped fee makes this unattractive late in the market but not impossible early.

The CU figure is an estimate, not a measurement. The band loop with u128 multiply-ceil and fee attribution over up to 32 buckets needs profiling. If it runs over, the fallback is to attribute fees by m_k only, which removes 32 multiplications.

goals_sacrificed: **LPs choose WHERE** is only half met. A zone decides whose fees you earn and where you are first-loss. It does not deepen liquidity at that price. True per-bucket depth inside one coherent cost function has no closed form: a bucket-dependent b_k needs a root-find over all buckets on every trade. Multiple overlapping pools would re-introduce static arbitrage between positions. I chose coherence and provable solvency over concentrated depth.

**TVL growth mid-market** is given up. LP deposits close at T_open and b is constant. Changing b mid-market breaks path independence. Combined with zone tranching it is exploitable: push the price at low b, add far-zone liquidity, then sell at high b, so the loss lands on other LPs' first-loss tranche. Rolling rounds that seed in advance are the substitute.

**LP exit before T** is given up. LP capital is locked from open to settlement and is only transferable. Withdrawing would cut b and require 64 ln calls to re-verify slack, or a very conservative bound. Horizons are 24h to 1 week, so I cut it.

**A new strike after the market opens** is restricted. Inside a market every band on the fixed grid of at most 64 buckets exists for free. Nobody can add a finer strike or split a tail bucket after creation. Each split costs b · ln 2 of extra worst-case loss and needs mid-market capital. Going finer means a new market and fragmented liquidity.

**Accuracy reward** is stepwise, not continuous. Payout is Δ × ring count at bucket resolution. One bucket outside the outer ring pays zero. A smooth distance kernel would need either parimutuel payouts (no fixed odds, no real exit) or per-bucket exponent ramps that one exp per trade cannot support.

**Composable positions** are weak. Trader and LP positions are transferable PDAs, not SPL tokens, because there are too many distinct payoff shapes to mint. Wrapping is possible, but this is not drop-in DeFi collateral, and that costs points in the hackathon category.

**Yield is not promised.** The design is honest that the LMSR LP is a bounded-loss subsidiser paid by fees. The TVL-and-yield story is weaker than a lending-style pitch. I traded it for a vault that is provably solvent in every outcome and a trader experience with fixed odds and instant exit.

**Existing building blocks** are only partly reused. The on-chain CLOB is unused. The binary LMSR's fixed-point math, fee splitting, quote-mint handling and oracle scaffolding are reused. The multi-bucket weight array, the ring trades and the tranche waterfall are new code.

**Small-capital creation versus a usable market** are in tension. Anyone can open a market with a tiny seed, but depth is proportional to the seed. 'Permissionless with small capital' and 'good prices' cannot both hold. The creator's 10% fee cut is the only bridge.

tests.note: The loss bound holds. But against informed flow, LP fees cover only 5-8% of the inventory loss. Informed volume caps near 2x F, not the 8-10x F the designer needs to break even. The tranche makes the near-the-money zone strictly dominated: the far LP gets the same share of any profit and no loss. Rational LPs pick tails, or do not deposit.

tests.numbers: A 1-unit LP that is the sole cover of a busy bucket (k*+3) collected 7.21 units of fees, a 721% return, which is 7.4% of all fees. Its maximum loss is 1 unit. With a full-range LP also covering that bucket, the dust LP gets 0.72%, i.e. pro rata.
tests.note: Fee yield is feeB[k]/Cov[k] with no cap, while first-loss is capped at F_j. Dust on uncovered hot buckets takes fees that would otherwise go to V.

tests.numbers: To move implied probability +10pp: single ATM bucket 0.046 to 0.146 needs 99.37 outlay (1.99% of LP capital); 5-bucket band 0.226 to 0.326 needs 124.11 (2.48%); the 'above ref' half 0.50 to 0.60 needs 200.27 (4.01%). Unwinding unopposed loses 1.97 / 2.46 / 3.97 (fees only). Unwinding after arbitrageurs restore prices loses 69.90 / 41.63 / 39.88.
tests.note: Works as an LMSR should, but it is cheap. Depth is b = 17.8% of LP capital because ln(1/pi_min)=5.63 with the floored 64-bucket prior. A 10pp move on a 5000-unit market costs about 2-4 units if nobody reacts. Do not use these prices as an oracle.

tests.numbers: N=64 default prior, b=8.89. A 20-unit buy moves the ATM line from 4.6% to 89.7% (+85pp) and pays 2.31x instead of the quoted 21.6x. The 3-bucket band goes 13.7% to 90.7% (1.83x vs 7.24x). The upper half goes 50% to 94.6% (1.27x vs 1.98x). Even a 2-unit buy moves the ATM line 4.6% to 23.6% (8.3x vs 21.6x). N=8 worked-example prior, b=15.5: a 20-unit buy moves the ATM line 22% to 78% (1.98x vs 4.5x). The LP's maximum loss is the full 50.
tests.note: The market opens and trades mechanically, and nothing reverts. But a 50-unit line is not usefully tradeable: one 20-unit bet consumes about 90% of the accuracy multiple. Usable depth needs F of roughly 100x the typical stake.

tests.numbers: Memecoin default grid delta=5% covers x0.21 to x4.71. +60% lands in bucket 41 (interior), and +45% / +75% calls land in 39 / 43, so they are distinguishable. The delta=2% grid puts +60% in bucket 55. The SOL-style delta=0.5% grid puts +45%, +60% and +75% all in bucket 63, a full collapse; the pool then loses 4965 of 5000 (99.3%) and both LPs lose 96-99%. P(tail bucket): Gaussian with correct sigma 0.011%; Student-t3 0.68%; t3 with true sigma 2x the guess 4.4%; Gaussian with sigma 2x the guess 5.3%, 3x the guess 19.7%. Stale prior: price drift during Seeding of 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 sigma gifts the first arbitrageur at open 1.1% / 2.5% / 7.5% / 22.4% of F after fees. The 1/256 floor alone costs b*KL = 53.5 units (1.07% of F).
tests.note: The market resolves meaningfully only if the creator's sigma guess is within about 2x. The grid and prior are frozen at create_market, and recurring markets sit in Seeding for a full round. A 1-sigma drift therefore hands about 7.5% of F to the first bot at open, every round.

tests.numbers: Operation-count estimate, not a measurement. Buy of a single line: ~88K CU. Buy with a 32-wide outer ring, R=4, as specified: ~227K CU; ~244K including the first-buy position create. Sell of the same shape with account close: ~230K. All are over the 200K target and well under the 1.4M cap. The fix of attributing fees on w>>64 (a u128/u64 division) brings the buy to ~170K; the designer's fallback of attributing by m_k brings it to ~136K. open_trading ~116K, claim_lp with a full zone ~113K, finalize ~46K, post_price ~22K. State is 3384 bytes (matches the ~3.5 KB claim); Position ~110 B. 9 accounts per buy (limit ~30). No instruction iterates over participants; every loop is over at most 64 buckets.
tests.note: The spec says 'at most 32 u128 multiplications'. That understates it: w reaches 2^120 and f^m reaches about 2^87, so products are about 2^207 and need U256 multiply-shift. Fee attribution as written needs a U256 division per bucket, which is the main CU cost. The PDA seeds include owner, but transfer_position rewrites owner, so an Anchor seeds constraint will fail after a transfer.

fatal_flaws: No flaw breaks correctness. Solvency, path independence and no-arbitrage all held under integer rounding in every run.

One structural economic defect cannot be removed without changing the mechanism. Against informed or public-price flow, the LMSR pool lost 22-25% of F per round (41% with sharp traders, 99% on a tail settle), while fees were about 2% of F. Informed volume self-limits at about 1.95x F, so fees cover only 5-8% of the loss. The designer's break-even of 8-10x F in volume needs uninformed flow, which the mechanism does not generate. Pyth-priced assets have continuously public information, so the subsidy is paid every round. LP yield is negative in expectation unless the protocol subsidises it or the pricing core is replaced (for example parimutuel, or a dynamic fee or spread tied to the oracle), and either replacement is a different mechanism. The designer disclosed this in direction; the simulation shows the size is about 10x fees.

The zone tranche makes the defect worse. The far LP got net 0.00 in the losing runs and the same pro-rata share of profit in the winning run, while the near LP took -41% to -47% for +2.3% in fees. 'Choose where to LP' therefore collapses to everyone choosing tails, or nobody depositing. This is a product-thesis failure, not a solvency failure.
fixable_flaws: VOID PAYOUT IS EXPLOITABLE. Redeeming at the frozen lock price pays the last buyer their marginal price on shares bought at a lower average price. Riskless profit was 15% / 42% / 51% of F for pushes to 0.5 / 0.9 / 0.99, whenever a void is predictable (an equity-feed T outside trading hours, which a malicious creator can choose, or a feed halt). FIX: store cumulative net paid on each Position (+8 bytes) and refund cost basis on Void. The sum of refunds equals V - F, so LPs get back F plus fees exactly. Alternatively redeem at the prior.

PRICE FLOOR BLOCKS EXITS. The w_min/S >= 2^-24 assert reverted 3 sells and 5 of 25 complete-set buys in a heavily traded market whose minimum price was 8e-8. A holder of a near-floor bucket cannot sell any amount. FIX: apply the floor only to buckets a buy pushes down (m_k = 0), and never on sells. Precision stays safe because w_k never falls below its initial 2^54.

STALE PRIOR AT OPEN. The grid and prior are fixed at create, and recurring markets sit in Seeding for a whole round. A 1-sigma price drift gifts 7.5% of F to the first bot at open (2 sigma: 22%). FIX: at open_trading, read Pyth and re-centre the grid and prior on the open price. Store the grid as log-offsets so that k* needs one ln.

DUST-LP FEE SNIPE. A 1-unit LP that is the sole cover of a hot bucket earned 721%, which was 7.4% of all fees. FIX: pay bucket k's fees only in proportion min(1, Cov[k] / (b ln(1/pi_k))) with the remainder going to V, or set a minimum Cov per bucket.
DIVIDE BY ZERO IN THE WATERFALL. When F equals Cov[k*] (every LP covers k*), the non-covering branch divides by zero. It needs a guard.

SAME-SECOND PYTH UPDATES (not simulated, reasoned only). Pyth's publish_time has one-second resolution, and several updates with different prices can share a second. 'Strictly earlier replaces' lets the first poster choose among them, which matters when the price sits on a bucket edge. FIX: require prev_publish_time < T <= publish_time, require VerificationLevel::Full, and define a deterministic tie-break.

ARITHMETIC UNDERSTATED. The weight update needs U256 multiply-shift, not u128. Fee attribution as written needs a U256 division per bucket and takes a 32-wide trade to about 227-244K CU. FIX: attribute fees on w>>64 (about 170K) or by m_k only (about 136K).
PDA SEEDS INCLUDE OWNER. transfer_position and transfer_lp rewrite the owner field, so seed re-derivation breaks. FIX: seed by (market, position_id nonce) or by the original payer.

DEPTH IS ONLY 17.8% OF LP CAPITAL with the 64-bucket prior floored at 1/256 (28 buckets sit at the floor, ln(1/pi_min) = 5.63). A 10pp move costs 2-4% of LP capital at risk and about 2-4 units if unopposed. A 50-unit market loses about 90% of a 20-unit bet's multiple. FIX: a lower prior floor does not help, because it raises ln(1/pi_min). Use fewer buckets (for example N=32) or merge tails, publish a minimum F in the front end, and do not expose these prices as an oracle.
A ZERO-VALUE POSITION THAT IS NEVER REDEEMED BLOCKS MARKET CLOSE AND THE CREATOR'S RENT. FIX: allow a permissionless close of worthless positions after settlement, with rent returned to the owner.
add_liquidity and remove_liquidity_preopen stay open after T_open until someone cranks open_trading. LPs therefore get a free look at the price. FIX: gate both on t < T_open.
ambiguities_you_had_to_resolve: Used the scratchpad directory, not /tmp/stook-attack-2, because the environment forbids /tmp unless the user asks; the contents are identical.

Default prior: a discretised normal on the bucket-index axis (8 buckets per sigma, tails folded into the end buckets), each mass floored at 1/256 and then renormalised. That gives pi_min = 0.0036, b = F/5.627, and 28 floored buckets.

Test 4 trader model: each trader draws a view v ~ N(truth, 7% of truth) and holds the belief N(v, the same sd) over buckets. They are risk neutral, trade once, and choose the single band (any width 1-32) with the largest expected profit. They size to the zero-marginal-edge point or to their budget (25, 100 or 400 units). They hold to settlement.

Test 4 fee and LP setup: flat 1% fee as the battery specifies, with the 1% to 3% ramp run as a variant. The near LP covers k* +/- 2 and the far LP covers [0,5], 2500 each. Ten seeds per configuration.

Test 4 was run on both the SOL-style grid (delta 0.5%, where a 7% sd is 14 buckets, so the traders are noise) and the memecoin grid (delta 5%, where a 7% sd is 1.4 buckets, so the traders are informed). Both results are reported.
A sell with a positive fee pays out |cost| - fee. Integer fee rounding: up on buys, down on sells. LP fee dust goes to the protocol.

Integer engine: exp and ln come from mpmath at 300 bits and are rounded one-sidedly as the spec says; f is a Q64 value. The engine models the rounding rules, not a specific on-chain exp/ln implementation.
Test 5 'unwind after arbitrage' assumes arbitrageurs restore the pre-attack prices exactly, by buying every other bucket by the same share count.
The Test 8 CU unit costs are my assumptions: U256 mul-shift 900 CU, U256 division 3.5K, u128/u64 division 1.2K, per-bucket scan 120, Anchor overhead 8K, create_account CPI 12K.
attack.summary:
I built and ran a float engine and an integer engine that emulates the on-chain rounding rules. The files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mohammadzakerirad-Sooth-soo--agents-analyze/3ab9aa51-1869-4558-827a-adf4e83ef8f5/scratchpad/stook-attack-2/: stook.py, t0_worked_example.py, battery.py, and the output in battery.out.

**What held**
- **Worked example:** it reproduces to every printed digit. I found no arithmetic errors.
- **Pricing core:** the designer's correctness claims held in every run, including under integer rounding.
  - Path independence: a 4 base-unit difference across orderings, and round trips cost the trader 2-3 base units, never a gain.
  - No static arbitrage: the best of 20,000 random portfolios after 500 trades was -0.0003.
  - Solvency: zero shortfall across all 64 outcomes, including a degenerate b=8 market and forced 2^120 rescales.
  - The LP loss bound held in all 70 informed-flow runs. The worst pool loss was 4965 of 5000.
- **Solana fit:** state is 3384 bytes, 9 accounts per trade, and nothing iterates over participants.

**What broke**
1. **Void payout.** Redeeming at the frozen lock price gives a riskless 15-51% of F to whoever pumps a bucket just before lock in a market that will predictably void. A creator can arrange that by choosing an equity-feed T outside trading hours. Fix: refund cost basis on Void.
2. **Price floor.** The 2^-24 floor assert reverts sells, so holders can be locked in. It also reverted complete-set buys partway through. Fix: exempt sells from the floor.
3. **Stale prior.** The grid and prior are frozen at creation while recurring markets wait in Seeding. A 1-sigma price drift hands the first bot at open 7.5% of F, every round (2 sigma: 22%). Fix: re-centre on the Pyth price at open_trading.
4. **Dust LP.** A 1-unit LP that is the sole cover of a busy bucket took 7.4% of all fees, a 721% return. Fix: cap a bucket's fee payout by how much of its maximum loss is actually covered.
5. **Compute.** A 32-wide trade as specified is about 227-244K CU, over the 200K target. The weight update needs U256 math, not the claimed u128. Attributing fees on w>>64 brings it to about 170K.

**The unfixable part is economic, not a correctness bug**
- Against informed flow the pool lost 22-25% of F per round, against fees of about 2% of F.
- Informed volume self-limits near 1.95x F, so the designer's 8-10x F break-even is unreachable without noise traders.
- The tranche makes it worse. The near-the-money LP netted -41% to -47% while the tail LP netted exactly 0 and kept the same share of any profit. Tail zones dominate, so the 'choose where' game collapses.
- When traders are pure noise (the battery's 7% sd on a 0.5% grid), LPs made +17.8%. LP return depends entirely on the ratio of noise flow to informed flow.

**Other observations**
- Depth is only b = 17.8% of LP capital. A 10pp move costs 2-4% of LP capital at risk and about 2-4 units if nobody reacts.
- A 50-unit market turns a 20-unit bet at 21.6x into 2.3x.
- A +60% move resolves fine on the 5% memecoin grid (bucket 41). On a SOL-style grid it collapses into the tail bucket and LPs lose 96-99%.

**Verdict:** sound-with-fixes as a mechanism, but it needs a subsidy to keep LPs. Build estimate: about 22 working days for two developers, covering the U256 fixed-point LMSR with certified exp/ln and property tests, the tranche waterfall, the Pyth settlement and void paths, the five fixes above, the SDK quote math, and the dartboard UI.

design.name: Stook Ladder: one 64-bin LMSR per (feed, T) with single-exp shaped trades
design.one_liner: Each (Pyth feed, expiry T, quote mint) gets one 64-bin log-spaced price ladder priced by a single multi-outcome LMSR. A drawn band or tapered "tent" line is one trade costing 1 exp + 1 ln. LPs fund the curve's depth b and earn fees. Solvency comes from the LMSR bound plus an explicit per-trade check. It reuses the existing exp_wad, ln_wad, wad_mul and wad_div math, the LP-seeding and fee-accumulator patterns, redemption, and the oracle-settlement scaffolding.
design.mechanism:
**Units**
- All token amounts are quote base units (u64). Decimals never enter the math.
- One share of bin i pays 1 base unit if the settled bin is i.
- WAD = 1e18 fixed point.

**Grid**
- N = 64 bins over log-price, anchored at P0, the Pyth price read on-chain at market creation.
- The creator picks step s from {0.25%, 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 4%, 8%} in natural-log units.
- bin(P) = clamp(32 + floor(ln(P/P0)/s), 0, 63).
- Interior bin j (1..62) covers [P0·e^{(j-32)s}, P0·e^{(j-31)s}).
- Bin 0 covers (0, P0·e^{-31s}). Bin 63 covers [P0·e^{31s}, inf).
- The tails make the partition exhaustive, so exactly one bin wins for any oracle price.
- Only the ratio P/P0 is used, so the 1e-8 to 1e5 price scale is irrelevant.
- Half-range is 31·s:
  - s = 0.5% gives +-15.5% log, for a large cap over a week.
  - s = 4% gives -71% / +246%, for a memecoin over a day.
  - s = 8% gives -92% / +1090%.

**State used by pricing**
- w_i: WAD, i128, equals exp(q_i/b), with 1 <= w_i <= 1e18. All start at 1.0.
- S = sum of w_i. Maintained incrementally with exact integer adds.
- b: liquidity parameter in base units.
- V: base units backing the curve. Fees are excluded.
- Q_i: u64, outstanding payout owed if bin i wins.
- Instantaneous price: p_i = w_i / S.

**Position shape (lo, hi, h)**
- Requires 0 <= lo <= hi <= 63 and 1 <= h <= min(8, ceil((hi-lo+1)/2)).
- Level vector: m_i = min(h, i-lo+1, hi-i+1) for lo <= i <= hi, else 0.
- h = 1 is a flat band. lo = c-h+1, hi = c+h-1 is a symmetric tent centred on bin c, and in between gives a trapezoid.
- A position of delta units pays delta·m_s if bin s settles.

**Trade**
- Inputs: shape and signed delta. delta > 0 is a buy. delta < 0 is a sell of units the caller owns.
- x = delta·WAD/b, with a required bound |x|·h <= 41 WAD.
- g = exp_wad(x). This is the only exp call.
- g^2 .. g^h are computed by h-1 wad_muls.
- For each i in [lo, hi]: w_i' = max(WAD, wad_mul(w_i, g^{m_i})), and w_i' <= 1e18·WAD is required.
- S' = S + sum over i of (w_i' - w_i).
- c = b·ln_wad(wad_div(S', S))/WAD. This is the only ln call. It equals C(q + delta·m) - C(q) for C(q) = b·ln(sum of exp(q_i/b)).
- Buy:
  - cost = ceil(c)
  - fee = max(1, ceil(f·cost))
  - the trader pays cost + fee
  - V += cost
- Sell:
  - refund = floor(-c)
  - fee = max(1, ceil(f·refund))
  - the trader receives refund - fee
  - V -= refund
- Q_i += delta·m_i.
- Final hard check: require(V >= max_i Q_i).
- Slippage limit: max_pay on buys, min_receive on sells.

**Why a shape costs one exp**
- Every q_i moves by an integer multiple m_i of the same delta, so exp(delta·m_i/b) = g^{m_i}.
- The cost depends only on S'/S.

**Path independence**
- c is a difference of the potential C, so reordering or round-tripping trades nets to zero before fees.
- Deviations are rounding only:
  - ceil on buys, floor on sells, less than 1 base unit per leg
  - stored-w truncation, relative 1e-18 per multiplication
- These are covered by the minimum fee of 1 base unit per leg plus 2f·cost.
- All 2^64-ish shapes are priced off one probability vector p. Any portfolio that pays at least X in every bin therefore costs at least X, so there is no static arbitrage.

**Fees**
- f = fee_bps/10000. The creator chooses 20..300 bps.
- 90% of each fee goes to LPs through acc_fee_per_share += fee_lp·WAD/L. The remaining 10% goes to protocol_fees.
- Fees sit in the same vault but outside V.

**Liquidity add**
- First deposit F:
  - V = F
  - L = F shares
  - b = floor(0.9999·F/ln 64), where ln 64 = 4.158883
- Later deposit D at any state:
  - k = D/V
  - b' = floor(b·(V+D)/V)
  - V' = V + D
  - shares minted = floor(L·D/V)
  - the LP personally receives an inventory vector vec_i = floor(Q_i·D/V), and Q_i += vec_i
  - w and S are untouched, so prices are unchanged
- This is exactly adding a parallel LMSR with depth delta_b = k·b at the same prices, where the new LP also buys that LMSR's outstanding inventory. The reasons:
  - C_{lambda·b}(lambda·q) = lambda·C_b(q), so V' equals the new potential.
  - Tracked liabilities stay equal to the internal q, up to safe-side floors.
  - Existing LPs' payoff in every outcome is unchanged, because (1/lambda)(lambda·V - lambda·Q_s) = V - Q_s.
  - The joiner is outcome-neutral at the moment of joining: vec_s + (k/(1+k))(V' - Q'_s) = D for every s.
- The rejected alternative is a pooled phantom inventory with mark-to-market share pricing. It allows buy -> add -> sell dilution of old LPs, and the simulation confirmed this.

**Solvency proof**
- Invariant: V >= C_b(q) >= max_i q_i >= max_i Q_i.
- Initially, C(0) = b·ln 64 <= 0.9999·F < V.
- Trades add exactly the change in C, rounded against the trader. Sells cannot take Q_i below 0 because units are owned.
- Adds scale V, C and q by the same lambda.
- The explicit require(V >= max Q) makes the property hold even under numerical drift. The 0.01% haircut on b is the drift margin.

**Settlement at bin s**
- Traders are owed Q_s in total.
- LPs split R = V - Q_s >= 0 pro rata by shares.
- Each LP also receives their own vec_s and their accrued fees.
design.state:
Three account types plus one token vault, all zero-copy.

**(1) Market PDA**
- Seeds: [b"mkt", feed_id(32), T(i64 LE), quote_mint].
- Fields:
  - feed_id [u8;32]
  - quote_mint Pubkey
  - creator Pubkey
  - p0_price i64
  - p0_expo i32
  - step_wad u64
  - open_ts i64
  - close_ts i64
  - T i64
  - fee_bps u16
  - status u8 (Open / Settled / Void)
  - settled_bin u8
  - b u64
  - V u64
  - L u64
  - acc_fee_per_share u128
  - protocol_fees u64
  - lp_residual u64
  - S u128
  - open_positions u32
  - open_lps u32
  - bumps 2
  - w [u128;64] = 1024 B
  - Q [u64;64] = 512 B
  - reserved 64
- Size about 1.85 KB, about 0.0137 SOL rent. Reclaimed by close_market when open_positions == open_lps == 0.

**(2) Vault**
- One token account, a PDA owned by the Market PDA.
- Seeds: [b"vault", market].
- 165 B, or up to about 182 B for Token-2022.
- Holds V + unclaimed LP fees + protocol_fees.

**(3) Position PDA**
- Seeds: [b"pos", market, owner, lo, hi, h].
- Fields: market 32, owner 32, lo u8, hi u8, h u8, units u64, bump.
- Size about 92 B, about 0.0015 SOL rent. Closed and refunded on full exit or redeem.
- Same-shape buys merge into the same account.

**(4) LpPosition PDA**
- Seeds: [b"lp", market, owner].
- Fields: market 32, owner 32, shares u64, fee_debt u128, fees_owed u64, vec [u64;64] = 512 B, bump.
- Size about 620 B, about 0.0052 SOL rent.

**Accounts per transaction**
- trade: 8 accounts (payer/owner, market, vault, user token account, position, mint, token program, system program).
- settle adds the Pyth PriceUpdateV2 account.
- No transaction touches more than 10 accounts.
- No instruction iterates over participants. The only loops are over the fixed 64 bins inside the single Market account.
instructions: create_market(feed_id, T, step_tier, fee_bps, seed_amount): permissionless. Requires T % 3600 == 0, T - now >= 1h, and seed_amount >= 10^decimals. The mint must have no TransferFee, TransferHook or PermanentDelegate extension. Reads a Pyth PriceUpdateV2 at most 60s old for feed_id and stores P0 and its exponent. Inits Market and vault, sets w_i = 1 and S = 64, sets close_ts = T - max(60s, 5% of duration), then runs the add_liquidity logic as the first deposit. The PDA seeds make (feed, T, mint) unique.

add_liquidity(amount D): anyone, while now < close_ts. First deposit: V = D, L = D, b = floor(0.9999·D/ln 64). Later deposits: shares = floor(L·D/V), vec_i += floor(Q_i·D/V), Q_i += the same amount, b = floor(b·(V+D)/V), V += D. Harvests the caller's pending fees into fees_owed before changing shares. One transfer_checked in.

trade(lo, hi, h, delta: i64, limit: u64): anyone, while now < close_ts. delta > 0 buys, with limit = max total pay. delta < 0 sells owned units, with limit = min receive. Computes 1 exp_wad, up to 7 wad_mul for g^2..g^h, one wad_mul per bin in [lo, hi], 1 wad_div and 1 ln_wad. Updates w, S, Q, V and the fee accumulators, then enforces require(V >= max Q). Init-if-needed or close the Position PDA. Exactly one token transfer, because fee and cost share the vault and are split by accounting only.

settle(): permissionless, now >= T. Takes a Pyth PriceUpdateV2 for feed_id with prev_publish_time < T <= publish_time <= T + 3600 and price > 0. This is the unique first update at or after T, so the caller cannot choose among prices. Computes settled_bin = clamp(32 + floor(ln_wad(P_T/P0)/step), 0, 63) with exponents normalised. Sets lp_residual = V - Q[settled_bin] and status = Settled. If instead now > T + 24h and the market is unsettled, anyone may call with no price: status = Void, prices frozen, lp_residual = V - ceil(sum of Q_i·w_i/S).
redeem_position(): owner, after settle. Settled: pays units·m_{settled_bin}. Void: pays floor(units·sum of m_i·w_i / S). Closes the Position PDA, refunds rent and decrements open_positions.

claim_lp(): LP owner. Before settlement: pays accrued fees only, shares·(acc - fee_debt)/WAD + fees_owed, which is the live yield. After settlement: also pays vec[settled_bin] + floor(lp_residual·shares/L), or the Void equivalent floor(sum of vec_i·w_i/S) + share of residual. Closes the LpPosition and decrements open_lps.

sweep(): the protocol authority withdraws protocol_fees. Once status != Open and open_positions == open_lps == 0, it also sweeps rounding dust and closes the Market and vault, returning rent to the creator.
design.lp_flow:
**Enter**
- Call add_liquidity(D) at any time before close_ts. create_market is the first add.
- Deposit D buys:
  - depth delta_b = b·D/V. For the first LP this is 0.9999·D/4.1589, about 0.2404·D.
  - shares floor(L·D/V)
  - an inventory vector vec_i = Q_i·D/V. This is zero for the first LP.
- The vector makes a late joiner exactly outcome-neutral at the moment of joining: they would get D back in every bin if no one traded afterwards. It also leaves earlier LPs' payoffs unchanged in every outcome, so there is no dilution and no buy-add-sell extraction.

**Earn**
- 90% of every trade fee, where the fee is f·|cost| on buys and on sells.
- Distributed pro rata by shares through acc_fee_per_share.
- Claimable at any time before T.

**Risk**
- An LP is the LMSR subsidiser for their slice of depth.
- Exact P&L at settled bin s, before fees: PnL = delta_b · ln(p_s^join / p_s^final).
  - p_s^join is the price of bin s when they joined. For the first LP it is 1/64.
  - p_s^final is the last traded price of bin s.
- They lose when the crowd ends up more confident in the true bin than it was when they joined. They gain when the crowd was wrong.

**Worst-case loss**
- max_s delta_b·ln(1/p_s^join) = delta_b·ln(1/p_min^join).
- For the first LP this is 0.9999·D, essentially the whole deposit, reached only if traders push the winning bin's price to about 1.
- It is always <= D, because ln(1/p_min) <= V/b.
- An LP balance can never go negative: payout = vec_s + shares/L·(V - Q_s) + fees >= 0.

**Exit**
- None before T. Removing depth would need lambda < 1, which can break q >= Q.
- At or after settlement, claim_lp pays vec[s] + floor((V - Q_s)·shares/L) + fees.

**Choosing where on the price axis**
- Not available inside a market. See goals_sacrificed.
- An LP chooses the market (asset, T). An LP can also reshape their own exposure client-side by pairing the add with band purchases in the same transaction.
design.permissionless_lines:
**A new line or band on an existing market**
- A "line / strike / range" is a shape (lo, hi, h) on the market's 64-bin ladder, not a new pool.
- Any of the 64·65/2 bin ranges, times up to 8 taper heights, is tradeable from the first second. No one has to open it and it needs no seed capital.
- Cost to the user:
  - the premium, about delta·sum of m_i·p_i
  - the fee
  - about 0.0015 SOL reclaimable rent for the Position PDA
- The UI maps a drawn band [a, b] to lo = bin(a), hi = bin(b), h = 1. A drawn line at x maps to c = bin(x) and a tent lo = c-h+1, hi = c+h-1 (default h = 4).

**A new market (asset, T)**
- Anyone calls create_market with a seed F >= 1 whole quote token, plus about 0.02 SOL total reclaimable rent.
- Depth is b = 0.24·F, so F = 100 USDC gives b = 24. That is thin but live.

**Why exactly one market per (feed, T, quote mint)**
- It is deliberate. Two independently priced ladders on the same feed and T would reintroduce static cross-market arbitrage against LP subsidies.
- The PDA seeds forbid it, and T is forced onto the hour so near-duplicate expiries cannot be spammed.
- The price the founder pays: the first creator fixes the step tier. The anchor P0 is taken from the oracle, not from the creator, so the grid cannot be mis-centred.
design.accuracy_reward:
There are three layers, all at bin granularity (step s in log-price).

**(1) Tent payout**
- A line at centre bin c with height h pays delta·max(0, h - |s - c|), where s = bin(P_T).
- This is piecewise-linear in log-distance from the settled price.
- With h = 4:
  - exact bin pays 4·delta
  - one bin off pays 3·delta
  - two bins off pays 2·delta
  - three bins off pays 1·delta
  - beyond that pays 0

**(2) Two traders staking the same money**
- The return multiple is m_s / sum of m_i·p_i.
- A narrower shape has a smaller denominator, so precision is paid more per dollar when right and paid zero when wrong.
- A flat band of width W at roughly uniform local price p returns 1/(W·p).

**(3) Better centre, same shape**
- Of two tents with the same shape and stake, the one whose centre is closer to s sits on a higher level m_s and is paid strictly more, until both are outside the shape.

**What it is not**
- Payout is not continuous in |P_T - x|. Within one bin all predictions are equal.
- A prediction that misses the shape entirely pays 0, however near it was in price terms.
design.trader_flow:
**Buy**
1. The user draws a band or line on the chart. The client maps it to (lo, hi, h), snapping to bin edges P0·e^{(j-32)s}.
2. The user enters a stake. The client inverts the cost formula off-chain to get delta: delta = b·ln(1 + (e^{c/b} - 1)·S / sum of w_i in band) for h = 1, or bisection for tents. It quotes payout-if-hit = delta·m_i per bin.
3. The client sends trade(lo, hi, h, +delta, max_pay).
   - The user pays ceil(cost) + fee.
   - The Position PDA [market, owner, lo, hi, h] is created or topped up.

**Exit before T**
- Call trade(lo, hi, h, -units, min_receive) at any time before close_ts, where close_ts = T - max(60s, 5% of duration).
- The user receives floor(C(q) - C(q - delta·m)) - fee. This is the same curve, so there is no counterparty search, and partial exits are allowed.
- An exit after someone adds liquidity gets less slippage.

**After settle**
- redeem_position pays units·m_s and refunds rent.

**Void**
- If the oracle publishes nothing in [T, T+1h], positions are paid at frozen mark-to-market: units·sum of m_i·p_i.

**Balances**
- A trader's balance can never go negative: they prepay the maximum loss, which is the premium.
design.settlement:
**Oracle read**
- Fully oracle-driven and permissionless. At now >= T anyone posts the Pyth pull update (PriceUpdateV2, verified by the Pyth receiver program, full verification level) for the market's feed_id.
- The program requires prev_publish_time < T <= publish_time <= T + 3600.
- The prev_publish_time condition pins the single first price at or after T, so the settler has no discretion over which tick is used. Hermes history makes that update retrievable later.

**Bin**
- ratio = (P_T·10^{e_T}) / (P0·10^{e_0}) as WAD, clamped to [1e-15, 1e15].
- settled_bin = clamp(32 + floor_div(ln_wad(ratio), step_wad), 0, 63).
- The on-chain computation is canonical. Clients use the same formula.

**Payouts**
- lp_residual = V - Q[settled_bin]. This is >= 0 by the per-trade invariant.
- Payouts are then pulled individually:
  - positions get units·m_s
  - LPs get vec_s + floor(lp_residual·shares/L) + fees
- The sum of trader payouts + LP vec payouts equals Q_s, and adding the LP residual gives V. The vault is exactly exhausted apart from floor dust, under every s in 0..63.

**Void path**
- There is no adjudicator and no dispute.
- The only non-price path is Void after T + 24h with no valid update, for example a halted feed.
- Void pays everyone at frozen prices: positions get sum of units·m_i·p_i, and LPs get sum of vec_i·p_i plus a share of V - sum of Q_i·p_i.
- V - sum of Q_i·p_i is >= V - max Q >= 0, so Void is also solvent.

**Compute**
- About 35K CU (1 ln, 1 div, account loads), plus the Pyth account read.

known_weaknesses: LPs are LMSR subsidisers. Their expected P&L before fees is <= 0 against informed flow, and the first LP's worst case is about 100% of the deposit. 'Yield' is fee income that must outrun delta_b·ln(p_final/p_join). At low volume LPs lose on average, and this cannot be hidden from judges.

The prior is uniform over 64 bins including tails. The first informed trader collects roughly b·KL(true||uniform), about 15-25% of the seed for a bell-shaped truth. Mitigation needs no extra code: the creator shapes the curve with their own trades in the same transaction as create_market.
Liquidity is thin per dollar. b = 0.24·F, so a 100 USDC seed gives b = 24, and moving one bin from 1.6% to 50% costs about 16 USDC. Depth cannot be concentrated where the price actually is.

One market per (feed, T, mint) means the first creator fixes the step tier and fee. A bad tier (too fine or too coarse) degrades resolution for everyone until T. The anchor P0 is oracle-derived, so it cannot be mis-centred, but it cannot be re-centred either if the price trends far before T. The open-ended tail bins absorb the mass and the market degenerates toward a binary.

Bin discretisation: payouts jump at bin edges, and a price 1 tick across an edge changes payouts by delta. Pyth confidence is ignored, so a wide-confidence print at T still settles. The first-update-at-or-after-T rule removes settler discretion, but a manipulated or outlier tick at T would still settle the market.
Late LPs receive a non-transferable, non-sellable 64-entry inventory vector, and all LPs are locked until T. There is no LP exit and no LP token, so LP positions are not composable collateral.
Positions are PDAs keyed by (owner, shape), not SPL tokens. They are not transferable without an extra instruction and cannot be listed on the existing order book.
Compute scales with shape width. About 45-65K CU for a typical 4-12 bin shape, about 110-130K for a full 64-bin shape at about 1K CU per wad_mul. Always under 200K, but not constant.

The numeric cap w_i <= 1e18 (q_i/b <= 41.4) rejects further buys of a bin already priced at about 1 - 1e-17, and |delta|·h/b <= 41 caps single-trade size. Large orders must be split or wait for more liquidity.
The fee is proportional to cost. Long-shot buys, which have tiny premiums and large LP liability, pay almost no fee relative to the risk they add.
Latency sniping in the final minutes before close_ts is only limited by the 5% / 60s lockout. LMSR loss stays bounded by b·ln(1/p), but late informed flow is pure LP loss.

Void after T + 24h pays frozen mark-to-market. A losing majority could try to suppress settlement for 24h. Anyone with a winning position can settle with one permissionless transaction, so this is weak, but it exists.
The same feed and T in two different quote mints are separate markets whose prices can diverge. This is not static arbitrage in one numeraire, but it is visible inconsistency.

Unknown Token-2022 extensions: the program rejects TransferFee, TransferHook and PermanentDelegate, but a mint with a freeze authority can still freeze the vault. The UI should warn on non-allowlisted mints.

**Trade**
- Typical 4-12 bin band or tent: about 55-70K CU.
- Worst case, a full 64-bin shape: about 125K CU. Always under 200K.

| Component | CU |
|---|---|
| exp_wad | 13K |
| ln_wad | 15K |
| wad_div | about 1.5K |
| g powers, up to 7 wad_mul | up to about 7K |
| Per-bin wad_mul, about 1K each (4-12 bins typical, 64 worst case) | 4-12K typical, 64K worst |
| max-Q scan and integer updates | about 3K |
| One transfer_checked CPI | about 5K |
| Zero-copy Market load + Anchor dispatch | about 8K |
| Position init or close | about 6K |

**Other instructions**
- add_liquidity: about 35K CU.
- settle: about 35K CU plus the Pyth account read.
- redeem_position, claim_lp: about 15-25K CU each. Void claims add 64 multiplications, about 40K.

No 256 KB heap frame is needed, because the program is zero-copy with no allocations in the hot path.
goals_sacrificed: LPs choosing WHERE on the price axis: sacrificed. One pooled depth b covers the whole ladder. Per-bin or per-range liquidity would need bin-specific b_i. That destroys the single-exp trick (N exps, about 830K CU at N = 64) and the closed-form bounded-loss and solvency proof. The alternative, independent per-strike pools or books, reintroduces static arbitrage between strikes, which the hard constraints forbid. An LP chooses only the market (asset, T). They can reshape their own exposure by pairing the add with band trades, but that is a trader position, not fee-earning range liquidity.

Continuous 'closer is better' accuracy reward: only approximated. Accuracy is rewarded at bin granularity (step s) through tent levels, max 8, and through narrower shapes paying higher multiples. Within a bin all predictions tie. Outside the shape the payout is 0, however close in price. A truly continuous distance-based payout needs either N exps per trade or a parimutuel pool. The parimutuel pool would kill pre-T exit and path-independent pricing.

Composable positions and LP tokens: sacrificed for state and code size. Positions and LP stakes are PDAs, not SPL / Token-2022 mints. 64 outcome mints per market would blow the account limit and rent. LP stakes carry a per-LP inventory vector, which makes them non-fungible. Other programs can hold positions through PDA signers, but nothing is a transferable token.

TVL / yield narrative: weakened and stated honestly. LP capital is a bounded-loss subsidy, not a delta-neutral yield source. LPs are locked until T with no early withdrawal, and expected return is negative without sufficient fee volume. Late-join neutrality and live fee claims help, but this is not an 'earn yield' product.

Permissionless grid choice: restricted. Anyone can open any shape for free and any new (asset, T) market with about 1 token of seed. But there is only one market per (feed, T, mint), its grid is fixed by the first creator's step tier and the oracle price at creation, and T must be on the hour. Permissionlessness was traded for the no-static-arbitrage constraint.
Small capital vs useful depth: in conflict. A small seed is allowed, but depth is b = 0.24·F, so a cheaply opened market has large price impact until others add liquidity.

Reuse of the existing order book and binary AMM instructions: not used. Only the WAD math, the LP-seed, fee-accumulator and redeem patterns, and the oracle scaffolding are reused. A CLOB per bin or per strike would violate the account-count and no-static-arbitrage constraints. The binary LMSR state does not generalise without the w-vector rewrite.
Exit between close_ts and T: not possible, because of the 5% / 60s lockout, and LPs cannot exit at all before T. 'A trader can exit before T' holds only up to close_ts.

tests.numbers: All trades: 5,000 seed, 6-decimal base units, integer model. The same 5-trade final position built in 3 different orders cost 234,425,214 base units pre-fee each time; spread 0. A band vs its two half-bands differed by 1 base unit. A tent with h=4 vs its 4 nested bands differed by 2 base units, and the stored w values were bit-identical. 11,269 buy-then-sell round trips were run in a randomised book, with sizes from 1 base unit to 5,000 tokens: pre-fee P&L was -1 base unit in 11,265 cases and 0 in 4, never positive. After the two 1-unit minimum fees every round trip loses at least 2 base units. Buying 1000 once and selling in 1000 pieces lost 503 base units; buying in 1000 pieces and selling once lost 498. The break: a round trip placed around someone else's add_liquidity is not path independent. At fee 1%, a front-run buy of 14.75b on one bin (outlay 12,859), a victim add of 5,000 into a 5,000 pool, then a back-run sell (receive 15,662) gives the attacker +2,802.57 net, risk-free, holding no position. The victim's 5,000 is then worth 1,520 if the bin loses and 5,420 if it wins; expected value under pre-attack prices is 1,581. With a victim add of 500 the attacker nets +140.57. If a 1% min_shares guard is added to add_liquidity, the best sandwich still nets +13.75 on a 49.6 outlay. Non-atomic version: a holder who paid 738.68 could exit for 724.05 before an LP joined and for 1,173.67 after, a 449.62 windfall paid by the LPs.
tests.note: The LMSR core is path independent down to rounding, and the rounding goes against the trader. The add_liquidity step is the hole. A joining LP buys a pro-rata slice of all outstanding inventory at the marginal price, and holders then exit along a deeper curve at a better average price. The spec gives add_liquidity no slippage parameter. This contradicts the designer's claim of no buy-add-sell extraction; they only tested the case where the attacker is also the adder. I reproduced that case: +972.01 if the bin wins, -527.95 otherwise.

fatal_flaws: LP economics cannot deliver the design's 'LPs fund depth and earn fees' premise. This is a flaw against that goal, not a correctness flaw. LPs are pure LMSR subsidisers and cannot place or withdraw depth. In the specified informed-flow test the first LP lost 13-29% of its deposit, with fees covering 3-40% of the inventory loss. It lost 91.8% once late traders (sd 0.3%) made the bin near-certain before close, and 97.7% when a +60% move landed in an edge bin. Breaking even needed volume of about 108x the deposit. A late LP bears almost no risk (+0.4% to +0.8%) and still shares the fees, so waiting strictly dominates seeding. Tuning parameters does not change loss = b*ln(p_final/p_join). Fixing it means a different mechanism, such as protocol-subsidised b, a parimutuel, or an order book.
fixable_flaws: add_liquidity can be sandwiched, and as specified the loss is severe. With no slippage parameter, an attacker netted +2,802.57 risk-free after fees from a 5,000 add into a 5,000 pool, and +140.57 from a 500 add. The victim's expected value fell to about 1,581 of 5,000. Fix: add min_shares or min_delta_b and a cap on the marked value of inventory received (sum of vec_i*p_i), and have the UI refuse to join books with spiky prices. With a 1% min_shares guard the residual sandwich was +13.75, so the tolerance must be tight; a guard on the price vector is better. There is a non-atomic remainder: any holder gets a windfall when an LP joins (449.62 in my run). This is inherent in selling inventory to the joiner at the marginal price.

Void pays at frozen marginal prices, so the last buyer extracts LP capital. A buy of 6b gave +765 profit on a 1,000 seed; a buy of 12b gave +980 and left the LP 1.31. This happens for certain on any feed that does not publish within T+1h, such as closed equity or FX hours. Fix: on Void, refund at cost basis by adding a net_paid field to Position and returning the rest to LPs, or use a TWAP or snapshot taken before close_ts. Also restrict markets to 24/7 feeds.

The existing wad_div cannot be reused as-is. Its 32-bit-chunk long division silently drops bits once the divisor exceeds 2^96; the first mismatch appeared at S~2^99 (a bin with q/b>27.2). In my runs this mispriced costs, and the V>=maxQ check reverted what would have been an under-priced buy. It also left the attacker's own units unsellable. Fix: use a true U256/u128 division, or cap w_i at about 1e10 (q/b <= 23) instead of 1e18. Note also that wad_mul(w, g^m) overflows i128 before the 1e18 cap check is reached, so the revert is a math error rather than the intended cap error.

Tier and fee squatting. The first creator fixes the step tier and fee for a (feed,T,mint) slot with a seed of 1 token. At s<=1% a +60% move collapses the market into bin 63. Fix: put the tier in the PDA seeds and accept cross-tier price divergence, or require a minimum seed of 100 tokens or more, or choose the tier from oracle volatility or confidence.

Cold start. b = 0.24 x seed, so on a 50-token seed a 20-token order moves a region by 60-80pp. Fix: set a minimum seed, let the creator shape the prior in the create transaction, and use fewer active bins (16/32) for small markets.
A sell reverts when refund < fee because of the 1-base-unit minimum fee, so dust positions cannot be sold; they can still be redeemed. Fix: set fee = min(fee, refund).
A 0-decimal or very-low-decimal mint with the minimum seed gives b=0 and a division by zero. Fix: require b >= some minimum.

A late LP's capital adds little depth. In test 4, 2,500 added after premiums had inflated V bought 118-321 of b, against 601 for the first LP's 2,500. Document this, or let LPs add depth without taking inventory by pricing the join at the curve.

CU. A full-ladder trade is 134-146K at 1K per wad_mul, but 235-253K if the 256-bit slow path costs 2.5K. Fix: benchmark it, cap the width, or pre-request a CU budget. Latency sniping in the last 5% or 60 seconds is pure LP loss. Fix: a longer lockout or a fee that rises near close. Pyth confidence is ignored at settlement. Fix: reject updates where conf/price exceeds half a step.

attack.summary:
The core LMSR survives the battery; the things I broke are add_liquidity, the Void payout, the existing wad_div, and LP economics. I wrote and ran an integer-exact Python model with the repo's exp_wad, ln_wad and wad_mul ported, plus wad_div in both an exact and a bit-for-bit form. The worked example reproduces to the 4th decimal, with 2 base units of vault dust.

**What held**
- **Path independence:** the same position built in 3 orders cost the same to the base unit, and 11,269 round trips returned -1 or 0 base units before fees, never positive.
- **Static arbitrage:** the best portfolio edge after 500 random trades was 0 base units.
- **Solvency:** worst shortfall was 0 across 36,000 fuzzed operations, all 64 settlement bins and the Void path. The V>=maxQ check never fired under correct math.
- **Solana fit:** an estimated 71-146K CU per trade from operation counts, 8 accounts, no loops over participants.

**What broke**
- **Sandwiching add_liquidity:** as specified there is no slippage guard. An attacker nets +2,802 risk-free after fees from a 5,000 deposit into a 5,000 pool, leaving the victim with an expected value of about 1,581. A guard on shares and inventory value reduces this to small amounts. It contradicts the designer's claim of no buy-add-sell extraction.
- **Void:** paying at frozen marginal prices lets the last buyer take 77-98% of LP capital. On a feed that does not publish at T this is guaranteed.
- **wad_div reuse:** the repo's division silently corrupts results once the divisor exceeds 2^96 (first mismatch seen at S~2^99, a bin with q/b>27.2). Costs were mispriced and an attacker's units were left stuck; the hard solvency check reverted an under-priced buy.
- **LP economics (structural, not fixable within this mechanism):**
  - The first LP lost 13-29% under the specified informed flow; fees covered only 3-40% of the inventory loss.
  - It lost 92% once the bin became near-certain before close, and 98% when a +60% move hit an edge bin.
  - Late LPs free-ride at roughly +0.5% and add only 20-50% of the depth per token. LPs cannot position on the price axis.
- **Thin markets:** 130 tokens move a region by 10pp against 5,000 of LP capital, with a 2.6-token unwind loss. On a 50-token seed a 20-token order moves a region by 60-80pp.
- **Tier squatting:** the first creator's tier decides whether a memecoin market resolves at all, for the price of a 1-token seed.

Verdict: sound with fixes as a bounded-loss, subsidised prediction market. It is not viable as an LP-yield product. Build estimate: about 15 calendar days for two developers, including the add guard, cost-basis Void refunds and a 256-bit division.

Cheapest to ship and the only design with a native tent payoff under the 200K CU target.

Same pricing core as the Ladder, and the best-audited one.

verdict.recommendation:
Build the Ladder core with Rings' liquidity lifecycle. There is one 64-bin log-price LMSR per (Pyth feed, T, quote mint, step tier), priced by one exp and one ln per trade. Settlement is by oracle only.

**Grid**
- N = 64 bins, step s from the preset table {0.25%, 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 4%, 8%}.
- bin(P) = clamp(32 + floor(ln(P/P0)/s), 0, 63). Bins 0 and 63 are open tails.
- P0 is read from Pyth inside open_trading, not at create. A rolling Seeding window then cannot go stale (Rings measured a 7.5% of F gift per 1-sigma drift).
- The tier goes in the PDA seeds, and the UI shows one whitelisted tier per asset class. Default to at least 2% for memecoins: at tiers up to 1%, a +60% move collapses into bin 63 and the LP loses 98%.

**State**
- w_i = exp(q_i/b) in WAD, starting at 1. Cap w_i at about 1e10 (q/b <= 23) so that S stays below 2^96 and the repo's wad_div stays exact. Add a property test against a big-integer reference.
- S is the exact integer sum of the w_i.
- b = floor(0.9999*F/ln 64), fixed at open. Require b >= b_min.
- V is pool cash excluding fees. Q_i is the payout owed if bin i wins.

**Position shape (lo, hi, h)**
- 1 <= h <= 8, and level m_i = min(h, i-lo+1, hi-i+1).
- A band is h = 1. A drawn line at bin c is a tent with lo = c-h+1, hi = c+h-1 and default h = 4.
- Payout is delta * m_s at settled bin s.

**Trade**
- x = delta*WAD/b, with |x|*h <= 23 WAD.
- g = exp_wad(x), and the powers g^2..g^h come from wad_mul.
- w_i' = w_i * g^{m_i}, floored at WAD. S' = S + sum of (w_i' - w_i). c = b*ln_wad(S'/S).
- A buy pays ceil(c) + fee. A sell receives floor(-c) - fee.
- fee = min(amount, max(1, ceil(phi(t)*amount))), so dust positions can still be sold.
- Q_i += delta*m_i, and require V >= max Q_i.
- Every trade takes a slippage limit. Every transaction prepends the 256 KB heap-frame request and an explicit CU limit.

**Fees**
- phi(t) ramps from 1% to 3% between T_open and T_lock.
- Split: 80% to LPs through acc_fee_per_share, 10% to the creator, 10% to the protocol.

**Liquidity**
- add_liquidity and withdrawal are allowed only during Seeding, gated on t < T_open. They are not gated on the open_trading crank.
- After open, b is constant and LP shares are locked until settlement.
- This removes the add-liquidity sandwich, the per-LP inventory vector and the late-LP free-rider.
- Recurring markets seed round N+1 while round N trades. That is the TVL story.
- A non-uniform prior is not program code. The seeder shapes prices with their own trades in the same transaction as the open.

**Lock**
- T_lock = T - max(5 min, 10% of duration).
- The reason is measured: 60 late sharp traders took the early LP from -26% to -92%.

**Settlement**
- Accept a Pyth update with prev_publish_time < T <= publish_time and full verification level.
- Reject the update if conf/price exceeds half a step.
- Apply a deterministic tie-break for updates sharing a publish_time.

**Void**
- Refund each position its cost basis from a net_paid field on the Position account. LPs receive the residual, which equals F plus fees exactly.
- Allow only 24/7 feeds, or reject any T that falls outside a feed's publishing hours.

**Settlement payouts**
- Traders redeem delta*m_s. LPs split V - Q_s pro rata, plus fees.
- Positions and LP stakes are PDAs seeded by (market, nonce), not by owner, so they stay transferable.

**Optional, week 3 only: \"choose where\" as fee-only zones**
- Each LP tags a contiguous zone.
- Fees are attributed per bin by m_k and paid as feeB[k]/Cov[k], with a minimum Cov[k] per bin.
- Losses stay strictly pro rata. There is no first-loss waterfall, so no zone is dominated and fee yield per unit of capital equalises across zones.
- It does not concentrate depth, and the UI should say so.

**LP framing**
- Present LP capital as a bounded-loss sponsor pool, not as yield. Protocol-seed the featured markets.

verdict.founder_goals_that_cannot_all_hold:
Eight of the founder's goals conflict, and the auditors measured each conflict.

1. **LPs choose where on the axis, against coherent no-arbitrage pricing under 200K CU.**
   - A per-location b breaks the single-exp closed form. Independent pools reintroduce static arbitrage.
   - All three attempts failed when measured:
     - Range-Tree range LPs added 0.0% depth, and their fees per unit of collateral fell as they concentrated.
     - Rings tail zones strictly dominated near-the-money zones (0.00 against -41% to -47%).
     - NLS zone LPs earned 0-5 fee units on deposits of 416-832.
   - Only a cosmetic version survives: fee-only zones, or an LP pairing a deposit with its own band trade.

2. **LPs earn yield, against a bounded-loss AMM on a publicly observable oracle price.**
   - LP loss is b*ln(p_final/p_join), and the outcome is revealed continuously.
   - Full-range or pooled LPs lost 13-47% net of fees under moderately informed flow in all four designs. Fees covered 3-40% of inventory loss. With sharp late flow or a tail settle the loss was 60-99%.
   - Informed volume self-limits near 2x TVL. Break-even needs 8-108x TVL in uninformed volume.
   - Yield is positive only when noise flow dominates: Rings LPs made +17.8% when traders were noise. Otherwise the pool needs a subsidy.
   - This conflicts directly with the TVL and yield pitch for the hackathon category.

3. **Permissionless small-capital creation, against a usable market.**
   - Depth is 0.18-0.24 of the seed across 64 bins.
   - In all four designs a 50-unit seed let one 20-unit ticket move a bin from about 1.6% to about 81%. The payout was about 3x against a nominal 64x.

4. **Exit before T, against LP protection.**
   - Every design needs a lockout before T. NLS's decaying liquidity makes late exits effectively impossible (383 marked, 2.62 recovered).
   - A longer lock cuts LP sniping losses but shortens the exit window.

5. **TVL growth mid-market, against path independence.**
   - Any change to b while inventory is outstanding was sandwichable. It was measured in three of the four designs. Guards shrink it but do not remove it.
   - Only liquidity that is constant from open onward is clean.

6. **Anyone can open any line or strike, against no static arbitrage.**
   - Arbitrary strikes need independent pools. Every sound design snaps to a grid fixed at creation.
   - A mis-set grid collapses a +60% move into the edge bin.

7. **Closer pays more, continuously.**
   - This needs N exps per trade, or a parimutuel pool with no exit. The achievable version is a staircase at bin width.

8. **Composable SPL positions, against low-KB state.**
   - There are thousands of payoff shapes per market, so positions are transferable PDAs, not tokens.

verdict.biggest_risk:
**Economic risk, not mechanical.**
- In every audited design the LP pool was a pure subsidy on a publicly observable price.
  - Fees covered 3-40% of inventory loss.
  - Seed LPs lost 13-47% per market under ordinary informed flow.
  - They lost 60-99% when sharp late flow arrived or the price settled in a tail bin.
- The recommended build does not change this. It only bounds the loss and keeps it honest.
- Without a protocol subsidy or sponsor budget for b, or without strongly noise-dominated retail flow, nobody rational seeds a market. "Permissionless lines with LP yield" then becomes empty markets, in which a 20-unit bet moves a bin from 1.6% to 81%.
- The hackathon pitch should lead with the draw-a-line consumer experience and protocol-seeded featured markets. It should present LPing as a bounded-loss sponsor pool, not as yield.

**Technical risk.**
- The fixed-point path is the second risk. The repo's wad_div silently truncates once the divisor exceeds 2^96.
- All CU figures come from operation counts; nothing was measured on-chain.
- Pyth pull settlement is new code. The existing program settles through an adjudicator.
- The week-1 CU and division gate exists to surface these before the UI work depends on them.
